title: Per-slice manifest (slice.yaml)
description: Canonical schema for the machine-readable per-slice manifest. Toolchain-neutral: a manifest written by an external generator (see `generator`) validates against it unchanged. essentials ships scripts/slice-lint.py, which parses and validates every slice.yaml against this schema and exits non-zero — wire it into CI or a pre-commit hook, because nothing in a JVM build reads a manifest and an unparseable one is invisible rather than loud.

^x-.$comment: Escape hatch. A project may carry toolchain- or project-specific data under an x- prefixed key without inventing a bare key that this schema rejects. No toolchain reads these; they are inert to every gate. Prefer a real field where one fits — an x- key nothing reads is documentation, not a contract.

schemaVersion.description: Manifest schema version, e.g. "1.3". Readers accept any 1.x, so a manifest stamped at an earlier 1.x stays valid and needs no restamp.

slice.description: Globally unique id <bc>.<slice-id>. kebab-case or snake_case; snake_case is REQUIRED on JVM platforms, where package directories cannot contain hyphens (e.g. orders.place_order).

generator.description: Which toolchain owns this manifest: essentials, manual, or an external generator. Determines whether lastSyncedAt/arch are expected and which tool may rewrite the manifest's derived fields.

language.description: Implementation language of the slice (open string: java | kotlin | typescript | python | go | ...). Lets tooling pick the right template family without sniffing file extensions in a mixed module.

status.description: Required lifecycle. 'shadowed' is the optional strangler-migration value, whose semantics belong to the external modernization tool that writes it.

notes.description: Deliberate limits and design constraints a reader would otherwise have to reconstruct from a comment — "no total count, because counting a filtered append-only log is a second full query". Human-owned prose, never derived and never overwritten. Not a changelog and not a TODO list: a note records a decision that is still true.

lastSyncedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC stamp of an external generator's last sync. Expected on manifests that generator owns; absent for generator: essentials, which has no periodic sync loop to stamp it.

sourceFingerprint.description: Hash of slice source inputs at last sync.

supersedes.description: Id of the slice this one replaces during a side-by-side migration — e.g. a rebuilt view projecting additional events, standing up beside the original while it catches up. The two are ONE slice in two versions: the superseded slice moves to status: deprecated and is deleted once consumers have swapped over. Tooling reads this link to tell a deliberate migration twin apart from two slices accidentally sharing a read model, and to report an outstanding retirement while both exist.

tier.description: The slice's EFFECTIVE architectureTier (open string: service-entity | cqrs | cqrs-es | layered-hexagonal | custom | future values). Consumers MUST NOT hard-fail on an unrecognised value — the required fallback is to behave as if it were `custom`. Note what that fallback costs, because it is silent: an unrecognised tier makes a tier-aware reader skip the slice's per-tier structure sections and its manifest generation entirely, so a WRONG value here is worse than an absent one. Write only tier vocabulary; the §R5 write style goes in `lane`. The owning BC's tier if the BC overrides it, else the project default; stamped so downstream consumers read the slice's tier directly rather than re-deriving it. When absent, consumers fall back to the project default. OWNERSHIP DIFFERS BY TOOLCHAIN, deliberately: an external generator with project data to derive it from may DERIVE it and overwrite it on every refresh. essentials has no such source, so it treats the field as human-owned and never overwrites one — /essentials:slice-check --adopt-tier backfills it only where ABSENT, and reports every slice it stamped.

lane.description: The owning BC's WRITE STYLE — where decision logic lives. essentials rules/slice-design.md §R5 sanctions exactly three, and a BC picks one and stays with it, which is why this is a closed enum: a fourth value is a change to the law, not to a manifest. This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from `tier` and the two must not be conflated. `tier` answers 'how is the backend organised' (the architectureTier vocabulary); `lane` answers 'where does the decision live inside it'. An aggregate-lane BC is event-sourced, so its tier is cqrs-es and its lane is aggregate. The two axes coincide on exactly one value, `service-entity`, which is what made the conflation easy to miss. Optional and essentials-owned: absent on projects that do not use the §R5 lanes.

profile.description: Set on integration-heavy / BFF bounded contexts.

serves.description: Query NAMES this view answers — ListOrders, not /api/orders. The route belongs in `endpoints`. The pattern rejects any value containing '/' because a route here is the single most common authoring mistake and is silently useless to every reader.

provides.description: Published read seams: an interface this slice implements and registers so OTHER slices can ask it a question without touching its store. The interface is declared in the BC's public `types/` surface; the implementation stays slice-private. This is the sanctioned way a read-owning slice answers a neighbour — see essentials rules/slice-design.md § Sanctioned sharing. Read-only by construction: a seam that mutates or decides is not a seam.

schedule.description: For a schedule-triggered automation. An automation declares `consumes` (event-triggered) or `schedule` (time-triggered) — at least one, and both where a process is driven by each.

externalSystem.description: External-system id; maps to external-systems/<id>/ (external_systems/<id>/ on JVM platforms). kebab-case or snake_case; snake_case is REQUIRED on JVM, where package directories cannot contain hyphens. Required for translation slices.

characterization.description: Optional strangler-migration metadata (parity oracle, etc.), owned by the external modernization tool that writes it.

tests.description: Coverage by type. Contract tests are the floor for translation/BFF slices.

arch.description: Optional event-model linkage, written by an external generator; essentials neither writes nor reads it. Ids take the form <boundedContext>/<sliceName>.

allOf.$comment: An automation is triggered by an event or by a clock — rules/slice-design.md § The four slice kinds lists the trigger as 'event / schedule'. Requiring `consumes` alone forced a schedule-driven automation to carry an information-free `consumes: []`.

A port-style ACL — the system calls out, nothing calls in — has no inbound message and therefore no mapping table, and is still unambiguously a translation slice. `consumes` and `maps` are required for every direction EXCEPT an explicit `direction: outbound`; with `direction` absent, both stay required.

name.description: The interface this slice implements, declared in the BC's `types/`.

note.description: What question the seam answers, and why it is a seam rather than an event.

consumedBy.description: Slice ids known to consume it. Advisory: a stale entry is drift to report, not a build failure.

path.description: ALWAYS quote this value in YAML. Inside a flow mapping an unquoted scalar containing '{' opens a nested mapping and the whole file stops being YAML — see essentials references/slice/manifest-guide.md §3. A mapping selected by a query parameter is written "<route>?<param>=".

auth.description: Coarse auth CLASS, deliberately closed so it stays comparable across projects and toolchains. It is not a permission model — a project with named permission bundles or per-resource scopes records those in `capability` alongside it.

capability.description: Project-specific permissions this endpoint requires — named permission bundles, scopes, roles. Open strings, because no two capability models agree. This is the machine-readable record of who may call the endpoint; `auth` is the class it falls into.

cron.description: Cron expression, as written in the source (e.g. a Spring @Scheduled(cron = "...")).

fixedDelay.description: ISO-8601 duration between runs, e.g. PT15M.

initialDelay.description: ISO-8601 duration before the first run.

note.description: Why this cadence — a schedule with no reason is the one nobody dares change.

via.description: Reader interface for cross-BC reads (mandatory cross-BC).

projection.$comment: additionalProperties is false here for a reason: `kind`, `handles` and `table` are the three near-synonyms an author reaches for, and each one would carry the event list under a key no reader consults — a manifest that looks maintained and reports the view as reacting to nothing. `from` is required for the same reason. `subscribesTo` is the fourth key authors reach for, and it is a DIFFERENT mistake with the same cost: it names the stream rather than the events, and its home is `aggregateTypes` — never `from`, which it would corrupt.

aggregateTypes.description: The event-store STREAM(s) this projector subscribes to — AggregateType names, PascalCase plural (e.g. Orders). This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from `from`, and conflating the two is the mistake this field exists to prevent: `aggregateTypes` is WHICH STREAM feeds the projector, `from` is WHICH EVENT TYPES its handler methods take. A stream name written into `from` silently corrupts the event list; an event type written here names a stream that does not exist. Optional: absent on service-entity-lane views, which have no projector at all, and on manifests authored before schema 1.3 — consumers MUST treat an absent value as unknown, never as none.

from.description: COMPLETE list of the event types this projector handles — the parameter types of its @MessageHandler/@Handler methods. A view declares its inbound events here and never in `consumes`. Event types only: the stream they arrive on is `aggregateTypes`.
